s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lip swelling with painful ulcerations in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: Progressive lip swelling with painful ulcerations
Lip edema with multiple superficial ulcers having heaped-up margins
key_facts: 34-year-old African American man
Hemophilia A
HIV-1 infection
Hepatitis C virus infection
3-month history of intermittent fever and unintentional weight loss
Progressive lip swelling with painful ulcerations
CD4 count rose from 94 to 160 cells/mm3 after resuming antiretroviral therapy
Lip lesions developed approximately two months after CD4 count began to improve
No hepatosplenomegaly
Undetectable HIV viral load
Undetectable hepatitis C viral load
Negative polymerase-chain-reaction assay for herpes simplex virus
Normal complement C1 esterase inhibitor levels
Negative Gram stain, acid-fast stain, and mucicarmine stain of lesion samples
